 TECHTALKS Retail Dollar Bonds RDB 3 Philippines 
 PDAX $200 dollar bond investment 
 Bureau of the Treasury dollar bonds 
 Retail dollar bonds available on PDAX app
 DT · 18 November 2026 · 4:00 AM PHT · 2 MIN READ 
 PDAX
 Text size A− Reset A+ Save Filipino investors can subscribe to the Bureau of the Treasury’s (BTr) third tranche of Retail Dollar Bonds (RDB 3) through the Philippine Digital Asset Exchange (PDAX) app starting at $200.
 The government-backed, US dollar-denominated bonds will be offered through the platform from 19 to 24 November 2026, allowing retail investors to earn interest in US dollars without opening a separate dollar savings account.
 PDAX said there would be no subscription fees during the primary offering, while the Philippine government would shoulder the withholding tax on interest payments.
 Also read GTA VI hailed as 'masterpiece' as critics award near-perfect scores 
 “Filipinos should not need substantial wealth or a private banker to access dollar investments. With as little as $200, they can now invest in Philippine government dollar bonds directly through the PDAX App, diversify their savings, and earn regular dollar income,” PDAX founder and CEO Nichel Gaba said.
 Also read

 Filipinos who missed the initial offering of the government’s 32nd Retail Treasury Bonds (RTB 32) can still invest through GBonds on GCash,…
 DT · 21 October 2026 
 Fully verified PDAX users can subscribe using Philippine pesos, US dollars or supported USD-denominated stablecoins through the platform’s conversion facility.
 However, investors funding their subscriptions through direct US dollar bank transfers must meet a higher minimum of $1,000.
 The previous retail dollar bond offering in 2023 carried interest rates of up to 5.75 percent annually. The final coupon rate for RDB 3 has yet to be announced.
 PDAX said investors would also be able to trade the bonds through its secondary market after issuance, although selling before maturity would depend on prevailing market conditions and prices.
 Also read Emirates Group profit plunges 66% 
 “Making investing accessible isn’t just about lowering minimum investments. It’s about removing the complexity that has traditionally kept ordinary Filipinos out of financial markets. That’s what we’re building at PDAX,” Gaba said.
 PDAX is licensed by the Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas as a virtual asset service provider, while government bond transactions are facilitated through its subsidiary, PDAX Securities Inc., formerly bonds.ph Inc.
